answer: Each identity must lock collateral in an escrow, so creating aliases does not dilute the cost of participation. When evidence links k coordinated identities to equivocation, pairwise-correlated penalties sum to O(k²), debiting their bonded capital; detection of a sybil swarm applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss under asymmetric depreciation. A vine of aliases therefore magnifies exposure, not influence: no zenith of rewards can offset the shared risk, and a prism of identities remains accountable through linked proofs.
